source_review.notes: Reviewed current official PostgreSQL checksum, pg_checksums, and amcheck documentation; current MySQL 8.4 doublewrite documentation; official SQLite atomic-commit and OpenZFS checksum documentation; the original FAST disk-failure and storage-stack corruption studies; ARIES; and the cited textbook. Eight of nine online destinations returned HTTP 200. The current MySQL page was readable in the research index but returned an automated-request HTTP 403. Engine behavior is version scoped.

evidence: Checked canonical page P, trusted address context A, algorithm/seed K, stored checksum c, bit width b, and opportunity count n.
Checked physical, logical, torn, stale, misdirected, latent, authenticated, scrub, quarantine, recovery-point, and false-negative terminology.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Checksum equality is bounded to canonical covered bytes/context and is never equated with semantic correctness or repair.

evidence: Recomputed all eight executable outcomes for valid, bit-flipped, torn, address-bound, payload-only, recomputed, and cross-page logical cases.
Recomputed 20 TiB at 100 MiB/s as 209715.2 seconds or about 58.25 hours.
Recomputed n/2^b for n=10^9 as approximately 0.23283 for 32 bits, 5.42e-11 for 64 bits, and 8.64e-69 for 256 bits.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Collision values are idealized union bounds under independence, not observed fleet risk.

evidence: Re-derived c=C_K(A||P_without_c) and identical canonicalization requirements.
Re-derived why trusted address context detects copied valid bytes while payload-only checks do not.
Re-derived why unkeyed recomputation passes and why two locally valid pages can violate a cross-page invariant.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No checksum algorithm, authentication construction, recovery implementation, or storage stack is universally proved.

evidence: Reviewed empty/uninitialized, wrong length/type/version, malformed offsets, single/multi-bit, zeroed, torn, duplicated, misdirected, stale, and truncated pages.
Reviewed checksum-plus-content rewrite, key compromise, RAM/DMA/kernel/controller/device faults, cache-path retries, correlated replicas, poisoned backups, and unsafe raw repair.
Reviewed cached versus media verification, scrubbing gaps, collisions, verifier bugs, format upgrades, encryption/compression context, and privacy of forensic pages.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Containment preserves evidence and prevents suspect state from silently serving or propagating.

evidence: Validated identical page/context acceptance, bit-flip and torn rejection, and address-bound misdirection rejection.
Validated payload-only misdirection and recomputed unkeyed corruption remain undetected by their stated check.
Validated local heap/index checks pass while the phantom identifier is caught by a cross-page invariant.
The repository verifier matched exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The model omits real formats, finite digest widths, storage, concurrency, recovery, and authentication.

evidence: Reviewed conditional checksum soundness premises and collision caveat.
Reviewed safe read ordering from I/O/length through physical integrity, header/bounds, then structural meaning.
Reviewed detection-containment-source-selection-repair-post-verification workflow.
Reviewed each exercise answer for arithmetic, failure coverage, and transactionally coherent recovery.
proof_review.notes: No absence-of-corruption, collision-free, self-healing, or production-recovery proof is claimed.

evidence: Separated detection from localization and repair; physical from logical validity; checksum from MAC/authenticated encryption.
Separated replicas/backups from independent verified recovery sources and finite scrubs from absence proofs.
Audited correct, valid, safe, proves, authenticated, repaired, and durable claims for explicit scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: All operational conclusions require named engine/storage procedures and recovery-point evidence.

evidence: The standard-library SHA-256 boundary model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
Eight online official/primary destinations returned HTTP 200; the current MySQL page was index-readable but curl-challenged with HTTP 403.
Front matter, section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and exact snippet expectations passed pre-review draft checks.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live database, RAM, filesystem, device, replica, backup, fault injection, scrub, power loss, repair, or restore was tested.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently separates page-byte integrity, identity/freshness, structure/semantics, adversarial authentication, detection latency, containment, and recovery.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed checksum coverage, read/write ordering, torn/misdirected/stale faults, structural verification, scrubbing, evidence, quarantine, recovery-source choice, post-repair validation, telemetry, and drills.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, eight-outcome executable model, ten distinct examples, and five progressive exercises move from checksum mechanics to production incident and integrity-program design.

limitations: Internal authoring, official/primary-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter does not certify any checksum/MAC, database, filesystem, storage device, replica, backup, recovery source, repair procedure, threat model, workload, or production integrity outcome.
